description.narrative:
Goal: The program goal is to accelerate the adoption of clean cooking solutions by the poor and underserved populations in Tanzania. This goal will be achieved through the following objectives:
Objectives: i. Catalyze the private sector participation in clean cooking solutions in poor population and underserved markets ii. Accelerate the uptake of clean cooking solutions through innovative financing mechanisms and technical assistance to selected private sector companies iii. Strengthen the clean cooking sector coordination and advocate for a conducive policy environment for a market led clean cooking sector.
Focus areas : Rural and marginalized communities in urban, peri-urban and rural areas
Target primary beneficiaries: • Poor people • Early and growth stage private sector enterprises through grant funding, business assistance and technical assistance • Business Member Organization including TAREA

Tanzania Clean Cooking Project (TCCP) är ett treårigt program som syftar till att förvandla den rena matlagningssektorn genom ökat deltagande från den privata sektorn. Programmet syftar till att ta itu med den dubbla utmaningen med utbud och efterfrågan genom innovativa mekanismer som förringar investeringar från den privata sektorn (utbudssidan) och gör rena matlagningslösningar mer överkomliga (efterfrågesidan).

The Tanzania Clean Cooking Project (TCCP) is a three-year program that aims to transform the clean cooking sector through enhanced private sector participation. The program aims to address the two-fold challenge of supply and demand through innovative mechanisms that derisk private sector investments (supply side) and make clean cooking solutions more affordable (demand side).

The annual narrative report presents progress in the implementation of project activities during the 2024/25 financial year, including highlights of achieved impacts, key challenges encountered, and lessons learned. By the end of the reporting period, AECF had contracted nine (9) companies, with two additional companies approved by the Investment Committee (IC) and expected to be contracted in October or November 2025.
The supported companies represent a diverse portfolio of clean cooking solutions, including improved household cooking stoves, large institutional stoves, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), and briquette manufacturing. During the reporting period, the companies received technical assistance in areas such as business formalisation, accounting procedures, marketing strategies, and reporting practices.
These support measures were intended to ensure that the companies were well prepared and adequately equipped to meet their objectives, thereby promoting a more structured, effective, and sustainable approach to achieving the programmes overall goals.
The annual narrative report provide summary of the key implementation highlights as follows:
Programme funding: The programme budget was revised in 2024/2025, increasing from USD 3.75 million to USD 5.2 million. This adjustment was accompanied by a oneyear extension of the implementation period and a revision of programme targets.
Programme spending: In FY 2024/2025, the programme utilized USD 1.4 million, representing 36% of the approved budget for the year and bringing cumulative spending to USD 2.06 million, equivalent to 39% of the total programme budget since inception. Programme spending refers to delivery activities, including allocations to competition management, performance monitoring, and staff salary costs. A total of USD 0.032 million supported Technical Assistance during the period.
Disbursements to Investees: In FY 2024/2025, a total of USD 980,202 was disbursed to investees, bringing cumulative disbursements to USD 1,144,920. This represents 35% of the funds allocated to investees and a share of the total available programme funding intended to flow through to investees. Matching funds: During 2024/2025 investees managed to raise an additional USD 468,053 in matching funds contribution.
The annual narrative report provide summary of the project results as follows:
Household Reach: During the reporting period, 119,496 households gained access to clean cooking solutions, bringing the cumulative total to 128,229 households. This achievement surpasses the project target of 90,000 households. The ResultsBased Financing (RBF) mechanism remained the primary driver of this progress, accounting for 71.2% of all households reached.
Institutional Reach: In 2024/2025, a total of 210 improved institutional stoves were distributed and are currently in use across 64 institutions, including 52 schools, two education centres, one college, and nine prisons. While this indicator was not part of the original project targets, it was introduced following a revision of project milestones during the year. The programme continues to prioritize companies producing and distributing institutional stoves under the ongoing call for proposals.
Employment & Income Generation: A total of 126 jobs were created in 2024/2025, bringing the cumulative number of direct jobs to 146, of which 49 positions are held by women. The cumulative wage bill now stands at USD 406,300.62.
Emission Reduction: The reporting period recorded 97,019 tonnes of CO2 emissions avoided, primarily through increased adoption of improved charcoal stoves. This brings the cumulative total to 100,800 tonnes of CO2 emissions avoided over the life of project.
Forest Conservation and Wood Savings: Reduced dependence on firewood resulted in 49,895 tonnes of wood savings, equivalent to the conservation of 4,561 HA of forest cover that would have been used for fuelwood.
Household Air Pollution: In 2024/2025, 597,480 people gained access to Tier 35 clean cookstoves, bringing the cumulative total to 642,195 people. This access has contributed to a 2150% reduction in exposure to harmful particulate matter, improving health outcomes for beneficiary households.
Matching Funds Mobilized: During the reporting year, investees contributed USD 468,053 in matching funds, bringing the cumulative amount mobilized to USD 555,706. The two companies contracted under the Results Based Financing (RBF) window i.e., Burn Manufacturing and Sayari Safi reported a combined leveraged investment of USD 2,865,733, comprising USD 2,195,127 from Burn Manufacturing and USD 670,606 from Sayari Safi. These figures are self reported and have not yet been independently verified. When aggregated with matching funds from other portfolio companies, the total matching funds leveraged to date amount to USD 3,333,786, representing 222.25% of the programmes targeted leverage.
Remarks: Despite delays during the onboarding of companies/investees, the project has achieved results beyond initial expectations. This performance confirms key Theory of Change assumptions, notably that once appropriate investees are selected and provided with targeted resultsbased financing and technical assistance, they are able to scale clean cooking solutions effectively. The results demonstrate that the causal pathway, from investee support to increased market delivery and adoption of clean cooking solutions remains valid, provided that implementation bottlenecks are resolved.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
